title: Lesson 1 — Greetings
topic: Greetings and polite first moves

phrases.en: Hello.
phrases.pt: Olá.
phrases.note: Use this at any time of day.

phrases.en: Good morning.
phrases.pt: Bom dia.
phrases.note: Use it before noon.

examples: Good morning.
Good afternoon.
Good evening.
pattern.contrast: Good the morning.

phrases.en: Good afternoon.
phrases.pt: Boa tarde.
phrases.note: Use it after noon.

examples: Good morning.
Good afternoon.
Good evening.
pattern.contrast: Good the morning.

phrases.en: Good evening.
phrases.pt: Boa noite.
phrases.note: Use it when you meet someone at night.

examples: Good morning.
Good afternoon.
Good evening.
pattern.contrast: Good the morning.

phrases.en: How are you?
phrases.pt: Como você está?
phrases.note: A common friendly question.

pattern.slot: the person or thing you ask about
examples: How are you?
How are your parents?
How are things at work?
pattern.contrast: How you are?

phrases.en: I'm fine, thanks.
phrases.pt: Estou bem, obrigado.
phrases.note: A short answer to How are you?

examples: I'm fine, thanks.
I'm good, thanks.
I'm a bit tired, thanks.
pattern.contrast: I'm fine, thanks you.

phrases.en: Nice to meet you.
phrases.pt: Prazer em conhecer você.
phrases.note: Say this the first time you meet a person.

pattern.slot: base verb: meet, see, hear from
examples: Nice to meet you.
Nice to see you.
Nice to hear from you.
pattern.contrast: Nice to meeting you.

phrases.en: See you soon.
phrases.pt: Até logo.
phrases.note: Use it when you expect to meet again.

examples: See you soon.
See you tomorrow.
See you on Monday.
pattern.contrast: See you the tomorrow.

objective: Greet someone, answer politely, and close a short first meeting.
pronunciationFocus: Keep greetings short and clear: HEL-lo, good MOR-ning, see you SOON.

dialogue.speaker: Ana

dialogue.speaker: Ben

dialogue.pt: Olá. Como você está?

dialogue.pt: Prazer em conhecer você também. Até logo.

comprehension.prompt: What is happening in the conversation?
How does Ana say she feels?
What do they say at the end?

productionPrompt: Greet someone for the first time, say how you are, and say goodbye.
retryHint: Use one greeting, one answer to How are you?, and one goodbye phrase.

title: Lesson 2 — Names
topic: Names and simple introductions

phrases.en: My name is Ana.
phrases.pt: Meu nome é Ana.
phrases.note: Replace Ana with your name.

examples: My name is Ana.
My name is Pedro.
My name is Carla.
pattern.contrast: My name Ana.

phrases.en: I'm Pedro.
phrases.pt: Eu sou Pedro.
phrases.note: A natural short introduction.

examples: I'm Pedro.
I'm Ana.
I'm Marcos.
pattern.contrast: I Pedro.

phrases.en: What's your name?
phrases.pt: Qual é o seu nome?
phrases.note: Use this to ask someone their name.

pattern.slot: the detail you are asking for
examples: What's your name?
What's your address?
What's your phone number?
pattern.contrast: What's your the name?

accept: What is your name?

phrases.en: Where are you from?
phrases.pt: De onde você é?
phrases.note: A basic question about origin.

examples: Where are you from?
Where are you going?
Where are you staying?
pattern.contrast: Where you are from?

phrases.en: I'm from Brazil.
phrases.pt: Eu sou do Brasil.
phrases.note: Use from for country or city.

pattern.slot: a country, city or kind of place
examples: I'm from Brazil.
I'm from a small city.
I'm from Cuiaba.
pattern.contrast: I'm from the Brazil.

phrases.en: I live in Cuiaba.
phrases.pt: Eu moro em Cuiabá.
phrases.note: Use live in with a city.

pattern.slot: the city or kind of place
examples: I live in Cuiaba.
I live in a small apartment.
I live in the city centre.
pattern.contrast: I live Cuiaba.

phrases.en: I'm a student.
phrases.pt: Eu sou estudante.
phrases.note: Use a before many jobs.

examples: I'm a student.
I'm a teacher.
I'm a driver.
pattern.contrast: I'm student.

phrases.en: This is my friend.
phrases.pt: Este é meu amigo.
phrases.note: Use this is to introduce a person.

examples: This is my friend.
This is my mother.
This is my father.
pattern.contrast: This is my the friend.

objective: Introduce yourself, ask a name, and say where you are from.
pronunciationFocus: Link short introductions smoothly: my NAME is, I'm FROM, I LIVE in.

What does Ana ask after Pedro says his name?

productionPrompt: Introduce yourself. Say your name, where you are from, and where you live.
retryHint: Use My name is or I'm, then add I'm from and I live in.

title: Lesson 3 — Countries and Cities
topic: Places, origin, and location

phrases.en: I'm from a small city.
phrases.pt: Eu sou de uma cidade pequena.
phrases.note: Use from to talk about origin.

pattern.slot: a country, city or kind of place
examples: I'm from Brazil.
I'm from a small city.
I'm from Cuiaba.
pattern.contrast: I'm from the Brazil.

phrases.en: Brazil is a big country.
phrases.pt: O Brasil é um país grande.
phrases.note: Big describes country.

examples: Brazil is a big country.
Portugal is a small country.
Canada is a cold country.
pattern.contrast: Brazil is a country big.

phrases.en: My city is hot.
phrases.pt: Minha cidade é quente.
phrases.note: A simple description with is.

examples: My city is hot.
My city is big.
My city is very quiet at night.
pattern.contrast: My city hot.

phrases.en: I live near the center.
phrases.pt: Eu moro perto do centro.
phrases.note: Near means close to.

pattern.slot: the place you live close to
examples: I live near the center.
I live near the station.
I live near my work.
pattern.contrast: I live near of the center.

phrases.en: The school is here.
phrases.pt: A escola fica aqui.
phrases.note: Here points to your current place.

pattern.slot: the place you are pointing at
examples: The school is here.
The hotel is here.
The bus stop is here.
pattern.contrast: Here is have the school.

phrases.en: The hotel is there.
phrases.pt: O hotel fica ali.
phrases.note: There points away from you.

examples: The hotel is there.
The bank is there.
The pharmacy is there.
pattern.contrast: There is have the hotel.

phrases.en: Is it far?
phrases.pt: É longe?
phrases.note: Put is before it to ask.

pattern.slot: an adjective you want to check
examples: Is it far?
Is it open?
Is it expensive?
pattern.contrast: It is far?

phrases.en: It is not far.
phrases.pt: Não é longe.
phrases.note: Use not after is.

examples: It is not far.
It is not expensive.
It is not difficult.
pattern.contrast: It is no far.

accept: It's not far.

objective: Describe a simple place and ask if it is near or far.
pronunciationFocus: Stress place words clearly: HERE, THERE, NEAR the CEN-ter, not FAR.

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.en: I'm from a small city.
dialogue.pt: Eu sou de uma cidade pequena.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.en: Is it far?
dialogue.pt: É longe?

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.en: Is the school here?
dialogue.pt: A escola fica aqui?

dialogue.speaker: Lia
dialogue.en: The school is here, and the hotel is there.
dialogue.pt: A escola fica aqui, e o hotel fica ali.

comprehension.prompt: What are they talking about?
Where does Lia live?
What does Tom ask first?

productionPrompt: Describe your city or neighborhood. Say one place that is here, there, near, or far.
retryHint: Use one full sentence with is and one location word like here, there, near, or far.

title: Lesson 4 — Be
topic: I am, you are, it is

phrases.en: I am ready.
phrases.pt: Estou pronto.
phrases.note: Use am with I.

examples: I am ready.
I am busy.
I am almost finished.
pattern.contrast: I ready.

phrases.en: You are right.
phrases.pt: Você está certo.
phrases.note: Use are with you.

examples: You are right.
You are early.
You are very kind.
pattern.contrast: You right.

phrases.en: He is my brother.
phrases.pt: Ele é meu irmão.
phrases.note: Use is with he.

examples: He is my brother.
He is my teacher.
He is my neighbour.
pattern.contrast: He my brother.

accept: He's my brother.

phrases.en: She is my teacher.
phrases.pt: Ela é minha professora.
phrases.note: Use is with she.

examples: She is my teacher.
She is my sister.
She is my boss.
pattern.contrast: She my teacher.

accept: She's my teacher.

phrases.en: It is easy.
phrases.pt: É fácil.
phrases.note: Use it is for things and situations.

examples: It is easy.
It is cold.
It is ready.
pattern.contrast: It easy.

accept: It's easy.

phrases.en: We are here.
phrases.pt: Estamos aqui.
phrases.note: Use are with we.

pattern.slot: where or how the group is
examples: We are here.
We are ready.
We are almost there.
pattern.contrast: We here.

phrases.en: They are busy.
phrases.pt: Eles estão ocupados.
phrases.note: Use are with they.

examples: They are busy.
They are here.
They are late again.
pattern.contrast: They busy.

phrases.en: Are you okay?
phrases.pt: Você está bem?
phrases.note: Put are before you to ask.

examples: Are you okay?
Are you ready?
Are you sure?
pattern.contrast: You are okay?

objective: Use am, are, and is in simple statements and questions.
pronunciationFocus: Do not drop the be verb: I AM ready, you ARE right, it IS easy.

dialogue.pt: Você está bem?

dialogue.pt: Você está certo.

How does Leo feel?
What does Mia say after Leo is ready?

retryHint: Check that every sentence has a subject and the right be form: I am, you/we/they are, he/she/it is.

title: Lesson 5 — Jobs
topic: Work, study, and simple roles

phrases.en: I work in a store.
phrases.pt: Eu trabalho em uma loja.
phrases.note: Use work in for a place or field.

examples: I work in a store.
I work in an office.
I work in a hospital.
pattern.contrast: I work in store.

phrases.en: I study English.
phrases.pt: Eu estudo inglês.
phrases.note: Use study before the subject.

pattern.slot: the subject, or when you study
examples: I study English.
I study at night.
I study on the bus.
pattern.contrast: I study the English.

phrases.en: She is a doctor.
phrases.pt: Ela é médica.
phrases.note: Use a before singular jobs.

examples: She is a doctor.
She is a nurse.
She is a manager.
pattern.contrast: She is doctor.

accept: She's a doctor.

phrases.en: He is a driver.
phrases.pt: Ele é motorista.
phrases.note: Use a before singular jobs.

examples: He is a driver.
He is a cook.
He is a teacher.
pattern.contrast: He is driver.

accept: He's a driver.

phrases.en: My job is simple.
phrases.pt: Meu trabalho é simples.
phrases.note: A simple job description.

examples: My job is simple.
My job is busy.
My job is interesting.
pattern.contrast: My job simple.

phrases.en: I need help.
phrases.pt: Eu preciso de ajuda.
phrases.note: A useful phrase at work or school.

examples: I need help.
I need a jacket.
I need two tickets.
I need a short break.
pattern.contrast: I need of help.

phrases.en: Can you help me?
phrases.pt: Você pode me ajudar?
phrases.note: A polite request.

pattern.slot: base verb: what you ask for
examples: Can you help me?
Can you repeat that?
Can you wait a minute?
pattern.contrast: Can you to help me?

phrases.en: Thank you for your help.
phrases.pt: Obrigado pela sua ajuda.
phrases.note: Use for before the reason.

pattern.slot: what you are thanking them for
examples: Thank you for your help.
Thank you for your time.
Thank you for waiting.
pattern.contrast: Thank you for to wait.

objective: Talk about work or study and ask for simple help.
pronunciationFocus: Keep request rhythm polite: CAN you HELP me? THANK you for your HELP.

retryHint: Use I work in or I study, then ask Can you help me?

title: Lesson 6 — Family
topic: Family and people close to you

phrases.en: This is my mother.
phrases.pt: Esta é minha mãe.
phrases.note: Use this is my to introduce family.

examples: This is my friend.
This is my mother.
This is my father.
pattern.contrast: This is my the friend.

phrases.en: This is my father.
phrases.pt: Este é meu pai.
phrases.note: Use the same pattern with family words.

examples: This is my friend.
This is my mother.
This is my father.
pattern.contrast: This is my the friend.

phrases.en: I have one sister.
phrases.pt: Eu tenho uma irmã.
phrases.note: Use have for people in your family.

pattern.slot: what you have, with its number
examples: I have one sister.
I have two brothers.
I have three questions.
I have one more stop.
pattern.contrast: I have a two brothers.

phrases.en: I have two brothers.
phrases.pt: Eu tenho dois irmãos.
phrases.note: Add s for brothers.

pattern.slot: what you have, with its number
examples: I have one sister.
I have two brothers.
I have three questions.
I have one more stop.
pattern.contrast: I have a two brothers.

phrases.en: My family is small.
phrases.pt: Minha família é pequena.
phrases.note: In English, family can be singular.

examples: My family is small.
My family is big.
My family is all here.
pattern.contrast: My family small.

phrases.en: My parents live here.
phrases.pt: Meus pais moram aqui.
phrases.note: Parents means mother and father.

examples: My parents live here.
My parents live in Brazil.
My parents live near the beach.
pattern.contrast: My parents lives here.

phrases.en: Do you have children?
phrases.pt: Você tem filhos?
phrases.note: Use do you have to ask about possession.

pattern.slot: the thing you are asking for
examples: Do you have children?
Do you have a smaller bag?
Do you have time?
pattern.contrast: You have children?

phrases.en: I don't have children.
phrases.pt: Eu não tenho filhos.
phrases.note: Use don't have for the negative.

examples: I don't have children.
I don't have a pen.
I don't have time.
pattern.contrast: I don't have not a pen.

objective: Introduce family members and say what people have or do not have.
pronunciationFocus: Make plural endings audible: sister, brothers, parents, children.

title: Lesson 7 — Numbers and Age
topic: Age, phone numbers, and simple quantities

phrases.en: I am twenty years old.
phrases.pt: Eu tenho vinte anos.
phrases.note: English says I am, not I have, for age.

examples: I am twenty years old.
I am thirty years old.
I am twenty-five years old.
pattern.contrast: I have twenty years.

phrases.en: How old are you?
phrases.pt: Quantos anos você tem?
phrases.note: The words are how old.

examples: How old are you?
How old are your children?
How old are they?
pattern.contrast: How many years you have?

phrases.en: My phone number is 555-0120.
phrases.pt: Meu telefone é 555-0120.
phrases.note: Say each digit clearly.

pattern.slot: the number, said digit by digit
examples: My phone number is 555-0120.
My phone number is 555-0148.
My phone number is on the card.
pattern.contrast: My phone number it is 555-0120.

phrases.en: I need two tickets.
phrases.pt: Eu preciso de dois ingressos.
phrases.note: Plural nouns usually add s.

examples: I need help.
I need a jacket.
I need two tickets.
I need a short break.
pattern.contrast: I need of help.

phrases.en: It costs ten dollars.
phrases.pt: Custa dez dólares.
phrases.note: Use it costs for price.

examples: It costs ten dollars.
It costs five dollars.
It costs too much.
pattern.contrast: It cost ten dollars.

phrases.en: I have three questions.
phrases.pt: Eu tenho três perguntas.
phrases.note: Questions is plural.

pattern.slot: what you have, with its number
examples: I have one sister.
I have two brothers.
I have three questions.
I have one more stop.
pattern.contrast: I have a two brothers.

phrases.en: The class starts at nine.
phrases.pt: A aula começa às nove.
phrases.note: Use at for clock time.

examples: The class starts at nine.
The class starts at eight.
The class starts at noon.
pattern.contrast: The class starts in nine.

phrases.en: I finish at five.
phrases.pt: Eu termino às cinco.
phrases.note: A simple time sentence.

examples: I finish at five.
I finish at six.
I finish at noon.
pattern.contrast: I finish in five.

objective: Use numbers for age, prices, time, and simple quantities.
pronunciationFocus: Separate number words clearly: TWEN-ty, THREE questions, at NINE.

title: Lesson 8 — Daily Routine
topic: Simple present for everyday actions

phrases.en: I wake up early.
phrases.pt: Eu acordo cedo.
phrases.note: A common daily routine verb.

examples: I wake up early.
I wake up at six.
I wake up late on Sunday.
pattern.contrast: I wake up in early.

phrases.en: I drink coffee.
phrases.pt: Eu tomo café.
phrases.note: Use the base verb with I.

examples: I drink coffee.
I drink tea.
I drink water with lunch.
pattern.contrast: I drink the coffee.

phrases.en: I go to work.
phrases.pt: Eu vou para o trabalho.
phrases.note: Use to before a destination.

examples: I go to work.
I go to school.
I go to the gym.
pattern.contrast: I go to the work.

phrases.en: I eat lunch at noon.
phrases.pt: Eu almoço ao meio-dia.
phrases.note: At noon means at 12:00.

examples: I eat lunch at noon.
I eat lunch at one.
I eat lunch at home.
pattern.contrast: I eat lunch in noon.

phrases.en: I study at night.
phrases.pt: Eu estudo à noite.
phrases.note: Use at night for the evening period.

pattern.slot: the subject, or when you study
examples: I study English.
I study at night.
I study on the bus.
pattern.contrast: I study the English.

phrases.en: I like music.
phrases.pt: Eu gosto de música.
phrases.note: Use like before things you enjoy.

examples: I like music.
I like football.
I like your idea.
pattern.contrast: I like of music.

phrases.en: I have dinner with my family.
phrases.pt: Eu janto com minha família.
phrases.note: With shows who is together with you.

examples: I have dinner with my family.
I have dinner with my parents.
I have dinner with friends.
pattern.contrast: I have dinner with the friends.

phrases.en: I sleep at eleven.
phrases.pt: Eu durmo às onze.
phrases.note: Use at for bedtime.

examples: I sleep at eleven.
I sleep at ten.
I sleep at midnight.
pattern.contrast: I sleep in eleven.

objective: Describe a simple daily routine with present-tense actions.
pronunciationFocus: Keep routine chunks smooth: wake UP, go TO work, AT night.

title: Lesson 9 — Food
topic: Ordering food and saying what you want

phrases.en: I'd like a coffee, please.
phrases.pt: Eu gostaria de um café, por favor.
phrases.note: A polite way to order.

examples: I'd like a coffee, please.
I'd like the chicken, please.
I'd like a table for two.
pattern.contrast: I would like to a coffee.

accept: I would like a coffee, please.

phrases.en: Can I have the menu?
phrases.pt: Posso ver o cardápio?
phrases.note: Use it to ask for something.

pattern.slot: the thing you are asking for
examples: Can I have the menu?
Can I have some water?
Can I have the bill?
pattern.contrast: Can I have to the menu?

phrases.en: I don't eat meat.
phrases.pt: Eu não como carne.
phrases.note: Use don't before the verb.

pattern.slot: the habit you do not have
examples: I don't eat meat.
I don't drink coffee.
I don't work on Sundays.
pattern.contrast: I no eat meat.

phrases.en: Is this spicy?
phrases.pt: Isso é apimentado?
phrases.note: Use is this to ask about one item.

examples: Is this spicy?
Is this fresh?
Is this vegetarian?
pattern.contrast: This is spicy?

phrases.en: The food is very good.
phrases.pt: A comida está muito boa.
phrases.note: Very makes the adjective stronger.

examples: The food is very good.
The coffee is very strong.
The room is very small.
pattern.contrast: The food is very much good.

phrases.en: Could we pay, please?
phrases.pt: Podemos pagar, por favor?
phrases.note: Could is polite in requests.

examples: Could we pay, please?
Could we order, please?
Could we sit outside, please?
pattern.contrast: Could we to pay, please?

phrases.en: The bill is wrong.
phrases.pt: A conta está errada.
phrases.note: A useful sentence when something is incorrect.

examples: The bill is wrong.
The order is wrong.
The address is wrong.
pattern.contrast: The bill it is wrong.

phrases.en: Everything was delicious.
phrases.pt: Tudo estava delicioso.
phrases.note: Was is the past of is.

pattern.slot: the adjective for the whole experience
examples: Everything was delicious.
Everything was perfect.
Everything was very quick.
pattern.contrast: Everything were delicious.

objective: Order food politely, explain a preference, and ask to pay.
pronunciationFocus: Soften polite requests: I'd LIKE a coffee, PLEASE; could we PAY, PLEASE?

retryHint: Use I'd like or Can I have, then add please. Use don't for one food preference if needed.

title: Lesson 10 — Directions
topic: Finding places in town

phrases.en: Excuse me, where is the bank?
phrases.pt: Com licença, onde fica o banco?
phrases.note: Start with excuse me to be polite.

pattern.slot: the place you are looking for
examples: Excuse me, where is the bank?
Where is the station?
Where is the nearest pharmacy?
pattern.contrast: Where is have the bank?

phrases.en: Go straight ahead.
phrases.pt: Siga em frente.
phrases.note: A common instruction in the street.

pattern.slot: the direction or the landmark you pass
examples: Go straight ahead.
Go left at the corner.
Go past the bank.
pattern.contrast: Go to straight ahead.

phrases.en: Turn left at the corner.
phrases.pt: Vire à esquerda na esquina.
phrases.note: At the corner marks the place.

examples: Turn left at the corner.
Turn right at the lights.
Turn left at the church.
pattern.contrast: Turn to left at the corner.

phrases.en: Turn right after the supermarket.
phrases.pt: Vire à direita depois do supermercado.
phrases.note: After means later in the route.

examples: Turn right after the supermarket.
Turn left after the bridge.
Turn right after the traffic lights.
pattern.contrast: Turn to right after the supermarket.

phrases.en: It's next to the pharmacy.
phrases.pt: Fica ao lado da farmácia.
phrases.note: Next to means beside.

examples: It's next to the pharmacy.
It's next to the school.
It's next to my office.
pattern.contrast: It's next of the pharmacy.

accept: It is next to the pharmacy.

phrases.en: It's across from the park.
phrases.pt: Fica em frente ao parque.
phrases.note: Across from means on the opposite side.

examples: It's across from the park.
It's across from the station.
It's across from the pharmacy.
pattern.contrast: It's across of the park.

accept: It is across from the park.

phrases.en: How long does it take?
phrases.pt: Quanto tempo leva?
phrases.note: Use this to ask about travel time.

examples: How long does it take?
How long does the bus take?
How long does the walk take?
pattern.contrast: How long time does it take?

phrases.en: It takes about ten minutes.
phrases.pt: Leva cerca de dez minutos.
phrases.note: Use about for an approximate time.

examples: It takes about ten minutes.
It takes about half an hour.
It takes about two days.
pattern.contrast: It takes about ten minutes of time.

objective: Ask for directions and understand a short route with landmarks.
pronunciationFocus: Stress route commands: go STRAIGHT, turn LEFT, turn RIGHT, next TO.

title: Lesson 11 — Shopping
topic: Shopping and prices

phrases.en: I'm just looking, thanks.
phrases.pt: Só estou olhando, obrigado.
phrases.note: A polite reply to a salesperson.

pattern.slot: the -ing verb: what you are doing right now
examples: I'm just looking, thanks.
I'm just waiting for a friend.
I'm just checking the price.
pattern.contrast: I'm just look, thanks.

phrases.en: How much is this?
phrases.pt: Quanto custa isto?
phrases.note: Use how much to ask a price.

examples: How much is this?
How much is the jacket?
How much is delivery?
pattern.contrast: How much cost this?

phrases.en: Do you have this in blue?
phrases.pt: Você tem isto em azul?
phrases.note: Ask about another color or option.

examples: Do you have this in blue?
Do you have this in a medium?
Do you have this in leather?
pattern.contrast: Do you have this in the blue?

phrases.en: Can I try it on?
phrases.pt: Posso experimentar?
phrases.note: Try on is for clothes.

examples: Can I try it on?
Can I pay by card?
Can I look around?
pattern.contrast: Can I to try it on?

phrases.en: It's a bit too expensive.
phrases.pt: Está um pouco caro demais.
phrases.note: Too means more than you want.

examples: It's a bit too expensive.
It's a bit too small.
It's a bit too heavy.
pattern.contrast: It's a bit too much expensive.

accept: It is a bit too expensive.

phrases.en: Do you take cards?
phrases.pt: Vocês aceitam cartão?
phrases.note: Ask about the payment method.

examples: Do you take cards?
Do you take cash?
Do you take euros?
pattern.contrast: Do you take card?

phrases.en: Can I get a receipt?
phrases.pt: Posso pegar um recibo?
phrases.note: Ask for proof of purchase.

pattern.slot: the thing you want handed to you
examples: Can I get a receipt?
Can I get a bag?
Can I get a discount?
pattern.contrast: Can I get to a receipt?

phrases.en: I'll take it.
phrases.pt: Vou levar.
phrases.note: Say yes, you will buy it.

examples: I'll take it.
I'll take two, please.
I'll take the blue one.
pattern.contrast: I'll take.

objective: Ask about price and size in a shop, then buy or say no politely.
pronunciationFocus: Stress the question word: HOW much is this? Do you TAKE cards?

title: Lesson 12 — Last Weekend
topic: Simple past for everyday stories

phrases.en: I went to the beach last weekend.
phrases.pt: Eu fui à praia no fim de semana passado.
phrases.note: Went is the past of go.

examples: I went to the beach last weekend.
I went to my parents' house on Sunday.
I went to a concert last night.
pattern.contrast: I go to the beach last weekend.

phrases.en: We had a great time.
phrases.pt: Nós nos divertimos muito.
phrases.note: Had is the past of have.

examples: We had a great time.
We had a long conversation.
We had a quiet evening.
pattern.contrast: We have a great time yesterday.

phrases.en: I saw an old friend.
phrases.pt: Eu vi um amigo antigo.
phrases.note: Saw is the past of see.

examples: I saw an old friend.
I saw a great film.
I saw my neighbour at the market.
pattern.contrast: I seen an old friend.

phrases.en: We ate at a nice restaurant.
phrases.pt: Nós comemos em um restaurante legal.
phrases.note: Ate is the past of eat.

examples: We ate at a nice restaurant.
We ate at my sister's place.
We ate at a small café.
pattern.contrast: We eated at a nice restaurant.

phrases.en: It rained on Sunday.
phrases.pt: Choveu no domingo.
phrases.note: Regular past adds -ed.

examples: It rained on Sunday.
It rained on Friday night.
It rained on both days.
pattern.contrast: It rained in Sunday.

phrases.pt: Eu não fiz muita coisa no sábado.
phrases.note: Use didn't + the base verb.

examples: I didn't do much on Saturday.
I didn't sleep well.
I didn't finish the book.
pattern.contrast: I didn't did much on Saturday.

phrases.en: Did you go out last night?
phrases.pt: Você saiu ontem à noite?
phrases.note: Make past questions with did.

examples: Did you go out last night?
Did you like the food?
Did you find the place?
pattern.contrast: Did you went out last night?

phrases.en: I stayed home and relaxed.
phrases.pt: Eu fiquei em casa e relaxei.
phrases.note: Regular past for everyday actions.

examples: I stayed home and relaxed.
I stayed home and watched a film.
I stayed home and cooked.
pattern.contrast: I stayed home and relax.

objective: Tell a short story about last weekend using the simple past.
pronunciationFocus: Keep -ed endings short: rained sounds like RAIND, stayed like STAYD, relaxed like RELAXT.

title: Lesson 13 — Making Plans
topic: Inviting, suggesting, and confirming

phrases.en: Would you like to grab a coffee?
phrases.pt: Você gostaria de tomar um café?
phrases.note: A polite invitation.

examples: Would you like to grab a coffee?
Would you like to join us?
Would you like to see the photos?
pattern.contrast: Would you like grab a coffee?

phrases.en: How about Saturday afternoon?
phrases.pt: Que tal sábado à tarde?
phrases.note: Suggest a time or idea.

examples: How about Saturday afternoon?
How about next week?
How about meeting halfway?
pattern.contrast: How about to Saturday afternoon?

phrases.en: Let's meet at seven.
phrases.pt: Vamos nos encontrar às sete.
phrases.note: Let's makes a suggestion for us.

examples: Let's meet at seven.
Let's take the bus.
Let's try the new place.
pattern.contrast: Let's to meet at seven.

phrases.en: I'd love to, but I'm busy.
phrases.pt: Eu adoraria, mas estou ocupado.
phrases.note: Decline politely with a reason.

examples: I'd love to, but I'm busy.
I'd love to, but I have to work.
I'd love to, but I'm away that week.
pattern.contrast: I'd love, but I'm busy.

accept: I would love to, but I'm busy.

phrases.en: Sounds good to me.
phrases.pt: Por mim, parece ótimo.
phrases.note: A casual yes.

examples: Sounds good to me.

Sounds fair to me.
pattern.contrast: Sounds well to me.

phrases.en: Can we make it a bit later?
phrases.pt: Podemos deixar um pouco mais tarde?
phrases.note: Ask to change the time.

examples: Can we make it a bit later?

Can we make it after lunch?
pattern.contrast: Can we make it to a bit later?

phrases.en: Do you want to join us?
phrases.pt: Você quer vir com a gente?
phrases.note: Invite someone to come along.

pattern.slot: base verb: what you are inviting them to do
examples: Do you want to join us?
Do you want to come along?
Do you want to meet earlier?
pattern.contrast: Do you want join us?

phrases.en: See you on Friday, then.
phrases.pt: Então, até sexta.
phrases.note: Close the plan with a day.

examples: See you on Friday, then.
See you on Monday, then.
See you on Saturday morning.
pattern.contrast: See you in Friday, then.

objective: Invite someone, suggest a time, and confirm or refuse a plan politely.
pronunciationFocus: Let invitations rise at the end: would you like to grab a COFFEE? How about SATURDAY?

title: Lesson 14 — Getting around
topic: Travel and public transport

Could you wait a moment?

examples: How long does the trip take?

title: Lesson 15 — At the doctor

productionPrompt: Role-play a phone call to reschedule an appointment. Say why you're calling, react to a problem, and ask for a call back.
retryHint: Start with 'I'm calling about…', use 'Could you hold on a moment?' or 'Could you put me through to…', and finish with 'Could you call me back later?'.

title: Example — Everyday Phrases
topic: Bundled B1 sample from the demo

phrases.en: She called off the wedding.

phrases.note: Phrasal verb: "call off" significa cancelar algo planejado.

examples: She called off the wedding.
They called off the meeting.
We called off the trip.
pattern.contrast: She called the wedding off of.

phrases.en: Sales have picked up this year.

phrases.note: Phrasal verb: "pick up" aqui é melhorar, aumentar.

examples: Sales have picked up this year.
Bookings have picked up since May.
Business picked up in the spring.
pattern.contrast: Sales have picked up of this year.

phrases.en: His career has really taken off.

phrases.note: Phrasal verb: "take off" = deslanchar, crescer rápido.

examples: His career has really taken off.
The channel has really taken off.
Her business has really taken off.
pattern.contrast: His career has really take off.

phrases.en: I give in; it's too difficult.
phrases.pt: Eu desisto; é difícil demais.
phrases.note: Phrasal verb: "give in" = desistir, ceder.

pattern.slot: the reason you are giving up
examples: I give in; it's too difficult.
I give in; you win.
I give in; let's do it your way.
pattern.contrast: I give up in; it's too difficult.

accept: I give in; it is too difficult.

phrases.en: If I can't read it, I'll look up the words.
phrases.pt: Se eu não conseguir ler, vou procurar as palavras.
phrases.note: Phrasal verb: "look up" = procurar (num dicionário, etc.).

examples: If I can't read it, I'll look up the words.
I'll look up the address.
I'll look up the schedule.
pattern.contrast: I'll look the words up of.

phrases.en: They didn't bring the subject up.
phrases.pt: Eles não mencionaram o assunto.
phrases.note: Phrasal verb: "bring up" = trazer à tona, mencionar.

pattern.contrast: They didn't bring up it.

phrases.en: Our supplies finally ran out.

phrases.note: Phrasal verb: "run out" = esgotar, acabar.

examples: Our supplies finally ran out.
The paper finally ran out.
My patience finally ran out.
pattern.contrast: Our supplies finally ran out of.

phrases.en: She knew the poem by heart.
phrases.pt: Ela sabia o poema de cor.
phrases.note: Expressão: "by heart" = de cor, de memória.

pattern.slot: what was memorised, and who knew it
examples: She knew the poem by heart.
I know it by heart.
He learned the lines by heart.
pattern.contrast: She knew the poem for heart.

phrases.en: I know the city like the back of my hand.
phrases.pt: Eu conheço a cidade como a palma da minha mão.
phrases.concept: like the back of my hand — como a palma da mão
phrases.note: Expressão: conhecer muito bem.

pattern.frame: I know ___ like the back of my hand
examples: I know the city like the back of my hand.
I know this neighbourhood like the back of my hand.
I know that street like the back of my hand.
pattern.contrast: I know the city like the palm of my hand.

phrases.en: So far, so good.
phrases.pt: Até agora, tudo bem.
phrases.concept: so far, so good — até agora, tudo bem
phrases.note: Expressão usada para dizer que, até o momento, está tudo certo.

pattern.slot: how things have gone up to now
examples: So far, so good.
So far, everything is on time.
So far, nobody has complained.
pattern.contrast: Until now, so good.

phrases.en: He was hitting on me.
phrases.pt: Ele estava dando em cima de mim.
phrases.note: Phrasal verb informal: "hit on" = dar em cima de alguém.

pattern.slot: who was doing it + on whom
examples: He was hitting on me.
She was hitting on my friend.
Someone was hitting on her at the bar.
pattern.contrast: He was hitting in me.

phrases.en: I'll get in touch with you tomorrow.
phrases.pt: Eu entro em contato com você amanhã.
phrases.concept: get in touch — entrar em contato
phrases.note: Expressão: "get in touch" = entrar em contato.

examples: I'll get in touch with you tomorrow.
I'll get in touch with the supplier.
Let me get in touch with them.
pattern.contrast: I'll get in touch you tomorrow.

objective: Use common phrasal verbs and idioms to talk about plans that change and results over time.
pronunciationFocus: Idioms are memorized as chunks with fixed stress: 'by HEART', 'the back of my HAND', 'so far so GOOD'.
productionPrompt: Tell a colleague about a plan that was cancelled and a project that is going well. Use at least three phrasal verbs.
retryHint: Use 'call off' for the cancellation, 'pick up' or 'take off' for the good news, and 'get in touch' to arrange the next step.

dialogue.speaker: Kayla

title: Lesson 22 — Making Arguments
topic: Debating and defending a position

phrases.en: While I understand your concern, the data suggests otherwise.
phrases.pt: Embora eu entenda sua preocupação, os dados sugerem o contrário.
phrases.note: While here means although.

examples: While I understand your concern, the data suggests otherwise.
While I understand the pressure, we can't skip testing.
While I understand your position, the timeline is fixed.
pattern.contrast: While I understand your concern, but the data suggests otherwise.

phrases.en: There's no denying that costs have risen.
phrases.pt: Não dá para negar que os custos aumentaram.
phrases.note: Admits an obvious fact before arguing.

examples: There's no denying that costs have risen.
There's no denying that the launch slipped.
There's no denying that demand fell.
pattern.contrast: There's no denying of costs have risen.

accept: There is no denying that costs have risen.

phrases.en: To be fair, both sides have a point.
phrases.pt: Para ser justo, os dois lados têm razão.
phrases.note: Softens a judgment to sound balanced.

examples: To be fair, both sides have a point.
To be fair, the team had very little time.
To be fair, the data is incomplete.
pattern.contrast: To be fair that both sides have a point.

phrases.en: That argument doesn't really hold up.
phrases.pt: Esse argumento não se sustenta de verdade.
phrases.note: Hold up means to stay valid under scrutiny.

examples: That argument doesn't really hold up.
That explanation doesn't really hold up.
The comparison doesn't really hold up.
pattern.contrast: That argument doesn't really holds up.

phrases.en: Let me play devil's advocate for a moment.
phrases.pt: Deixa eu fazer o advogado do diabo por um momento.
phrases.note: Argue the opposite side on purpose.

pattern.slot: base verb: what you offer to do
examples: Let me play devil's advocate for a moment.
Let me put the other case.
Let me check the numbers first.
pattern.contrast: Let me to play devil's advocate.

phrases.en: I'd argue that the opposite is true.
phrases.pt: Eu diria que o oposto é verdade.
phrases.note: A confident way to state a claim.

pattern.slot: your claim, as a full clause
examples: I'd argue that the opposite is true.
I'd argue that the risk is overstated.
I'd argue that we already have the answer.
pattern.contrast: I'd argue the opposite is true that.

accept: I would argue that the opposite is true.

phrases.en: That's beside the point.
phrases.pt: Isso foge do assunto.
phrases.note: Means not relevant to the issue.

pattern.slot: the thing you are setting aside
examples: That's beside the point.
The cost is beside the point.
Whose idea it was is beside the point.
pattern.contrast: That's outside of the point.

accept: That is beside the point.

phrases.en: Ultimately, it comes down to priorities.
phrases.pt: No fim das contas, tudo se resume a prioridades.
phrases.note: Come down to means the key factor is.

pattern.slot: the thing the decision really turns on
examples: Ultimately, it comes down to priorities.
In the end, it comes down to cost.
It comes down to who owns the decision.
pattern.contrast: Ultimately, it comes down of priorities.

objective: Defend a position in a discussion: concede fairly, challenge weak reasoning, and steer back to what matters.
pronunciationFocus: Stress the pivot word that turns the sentence: 'the DATA suggests otherwise', 'that's beSIDE the point'.
productionPrompt: Argue for or against delaying a decision at work. Concede one point to the other side, then explain why your position still holds.
retryHint: Use 'While I understand…, the data suggests…', concede with 'To be fair…', and close with 'Ultimately, it comes down to…'.

dialogue.speaker: Iris
dialogue.en: We should delay the launch until the reviews are perfect.
dialogue.pt: A gente devia adiar o lançamento até as avaliações estarem perfeitas.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.en: While I understand your concern, the data suggests otherwise. Early users forgive small bugs.
dialogue.pt: Embora eu entenda sua preocupação, os dados indicam o contrário. Os primeiros usuários perdoam pequenos bugs.

dialogue.speaker: Iris

dialogue.pt: Mas não dá para negar que uma primeira impressão ruim fica marcada.

dialogue.en: To be fair, that's a real risk. Let me play devil's advocate: what does waiting actually buy us?
dialogue.pt: Para ser justo, esse risco é real. Deixa eu fazer de advogado do diabo: o que esperar realmente nos dá?

dialogue.speaker: Iris
dialogue.en: Time to fix the onboarding flow.
dialogue.pt: Tempo para consertar o fluxo de integração.

dialogue.speaker: Omar
dialogue.en: That argument doesn't really hold up — we can ship that as an update. Ultimately it comes down to priorities.

options: Whether to delay the product launch
How much to charge for the product

options: The onboarding fix can ship later as an update

title: Lesson 23 — Hypotheticals
topic: Conditionals and unreal situations

phrases.en: If I were you, I'd take the offer.
phrases.pt: Se eu fosse você, aceitaria a oferta.
phrases.note: Use were for all subjects in this pattern.

examples: If I were you, I'd take the offer.
If I were you, I'd wait a week.
If I were you, I'd ask for more detail.
pattern.contrast: If I was you, I'd take the offer.

accept: If I were you, I would take the offer.

phrases.en: Had I known, I would have helped.
phrases.pt: Se eu soubesse, teria ajudado.
phrases.note: Had + subject replaces if in formal speech.

pattern.slot: past participle twice: the missed condition, then the missed result
examples: Had I known, I would have helped.
Had I seen the email, I would have replied.
Had I asked earlier, I would have got a place.
pattern.contrast: Had I knew, I would have helped.

accept: Had I known, I'd have helped.

phrases.en: Unless we act now, we'll lose the deal.
phrases.pt: A não ser que a gente aja agora, vamos perder o negócio.
phrases.note: Unless means if not.

examples: Unless we act now, we'll lose the deal.
Unless the supplier confirms, we'll change the plan.
Unless costs fall, we'll have to raise prices.
pattern.contrast: Unless we don't act now, we'll lose the deal.

phrases.en: Suppose the budget gets cut.
phrases.pt: Suponha que o orçamento seja cortado.
phrases.note: Suppose introduces a hypothetical case.

pattern.slot: the hypothetical, as a full clause
examples: Suppose the budget gets cut.
Suppose the client says no.
Suppose we run the trial for a month.
pattern.contrast: Suppose of the budget gets cut.

phrases.en: I wish I had more time.
phrases.pt: Eu queria ter mais tempo.
phrases.note: Wish + past tense shows present regret.

examples: I wish I had more time.
I wish I had more information.
I wish I had a better answer.
pattern.contrast: I wish I have more time.

phrases.en: If only I had saved more money.
phrases.pt: Se eu ao menos tivesse economizado mais dinheiro.
phrases.note: If only adds emotion to a regret.

examples: If only I had saved more money.
If only I had started earlier.
If only I had asked.
pattern.contrast: If only I had save more money.

phrases.en: Even if it rains, we'll still go.
phrases.pt: Mesmo que chova, a gente vai assim mesmo.
phrases.note: Even if stresses that the result won't change.

pattern.slot: the obstacle, then what happens anyway
examples: Even if it rains, we'll still go.
Even if the numbers improve, we'll still review it.
Even if they refuse, we'll still submit it.
pattern.contrast: Even if it will rain, we'll still go.

phrases.en: Otherwise, we would have missed the flight.
phrases.pt: Caso contrário, teríamos perdido o voo.
phrases.note: Otherwise means if that had not happened.

examples: Otherwise, we would have missed the flight.
Otherwise, they would have cancelled the order.
Otherwise, I would have waited outside.
pattern.contrast: Otherwise, we had missed the flight.

accept: Otherwise, we'd have missed the flight.

objective: Discuss unreal and hypothetical situations with second and third conditionals, 'unless', 'even if', and 'wish'.
pronunciationFocus: Contracted 'would' and 'had' almost disappear: 'I'd take it', 'had I known' — the vowel carries the meaning.
productionPrompt: Describe a decision you once faced. Say what you would do differently now, and give one piece of advice using 'If I were you…'.
retryHint: Use the third conditional for regret ('If only I had…', 'Had I known…') and the second conditional for advice ('If I were you, I'd…').

dialogue.speaker: Théo

options: Whether to accept a job transfer to Lisbon
Whether to ask for a pay rise
Whether to move in with Rania

title: Lesson 24 — Negotiating
topic: Reaching an agreement

phrases.en: Let's try to find some middle ground.
phrases.pt: Vamos tentar encontrar um meio-termo.
phrases.note: A compromise both sides accept.

examples: Let's try to find some middle ground.
Let's not get ahead of ourselves.
Let's take a short break.
pattern.contrast: Let's to find some middle ground.

phrases.en: Would you be willing to compromise?
phrases.pt: Você estaria disposto a ceder um pouco?
phrases.note: Asks if someone is open to giving in.

pattern.slot: base verb: the concession you ask for
examples: Would you be willing to compromise?
Would you be willing to split the difference?
Would you be willing to start in June?
pattern.contrast: Would you be willing compromise?

phrases.en: That works for me.
phrases.pt: Por mim, tudo bem.
phrases.note: A casual way to accept a proposal.

examples: That works for me.
That works for us.
That works for the whole team.
pattern.contrast: That works to me.

phrases.en: I'm afraid that's out of the question.
phrases.pt: Receio que isso esteja fora de cogitação.
phrases.note: A firm but polite refusal.

examples: I'm afraid that's out of the question.
I'm afraid we can't move on price.
I'm afraid that date doesn't work.
pattern.contrast: I'm afraid of that's out of the question.

accept: I'm afraid that is out of the question.

phrases.en: Can we meet halfway on the price?
phrases.pt: Podemos chegar a um meio-termo no preço?
phrases.note: Both sides give up a little.

pattern.slot: base verb: what you propose doing together
examples: Can we meet halfway on the price?
Can we revisit the timeline?
Can we look at the numbers again?
pattern.contrast: Can we to meet halfway on the price?

phrases.en: Let's not get ahead of ourselves.
phrases.pt: Não vamos nos adiantar.
phrases.note: Means don't assume too much too soon.

examples: Let's try to find some middle ground.
Let's not get ahead of ourselves.
Let's take a short break.
pattern.contrast: Let's to find some middle ground.

phrases.en: I'll see what I can do.
phrases.pt: Vou ver o que posso fazer.
phrases.note: A soft promise without committing.

pattern.slot: the clause you are hedging with
examples: I'll see what I can do.
I'll see what the team says.
I'll see what is possible before Friday.
pattern.contrast: I'll see what can I do.

phrases.en: So, do we have a deal?
phrases.pt: Então, temos um acordo?
phrases.note: Used to close a negotiation.

pattern.slot: what you are trying to close on
examples: So, do we have a deal?
So, do we have an agreement?
So, do we have a date?
pattern.contrast: So, we have a deal?

objective: Move a negotiation toward agreement: signal flexibility, refuse firmly where needed, and close the deal.
pronunciationFocus: Soften a refusal with a falling, unhurried tone: 'I'm afraid that's out of the question' — no sharp stress.
productionPrompt: Role-play a negotiation over a price or deadline. Make one firm refusal, offer one trade, and close with a clear agreement.
retryHint: Offer flexibility with 'Would you be willing to…' and 'meet halfway', refuse with 'I'm afraid that's out of the question', and close with 'Do we have a deal?'.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.en: Faster delivery would help. Let's not get ahead of ourselves, though — what about payment terms?
dialogue.pt: Uma entrega mais rápida ajudaria. Mas vamos com calma — e as condições de pagamento?

dialogue.speaker: Sami
dialogue.en: Sixty days instead of thirty, if we settle on six percent.
dialogue.pt: Sessenta dias em vez de trinta, se fecharmos em seis por cento.

dialogue.speaker: Nora
dialogue.en: That works for me. Do we have a deal?
dialogue.pt: Por mim está ótimo. Fechado?

comprehension.prompt: What are Sami and Nora negotiating?
options: The terms of a supply contract
comprehension.answer: The terms of a supply contract

comprehension.prompt: Which request does Sami firmly reject?
What do they finally agree on?
options: Six percent off with faster delivery and sixty-day terms
Five percent off with no other changes
comprehension.answer: Six percent off with faster delivery and sixty-day terms

title: Lesson 25 — Trends and Data
topic: Describing changes and numbers

phrases.en: Sales have soared over the past quarter.
phrases.pt: As vendas dispararam no último trimestre.
phrases.note: Soar means to rise sharply.

examples: Sales have soared over the past quarter.
Costs have soared over the last year.
Enquiries have soared over the summer.
pattern.contrast: Sales have soared in the past quarter of.

phrases.en: There's been a sharp decline in demand.
phrases.pt: Houve uma queda acentuada na demanda.
phrases.note: A strong, sudden drop.

pattern.slot: the size and direction of the change, then what changed
examples: There's been a sharp decline in demand.
There's been a steady rise in costs.
There's been a small increase in traffic.
pattern.contrast: There's been a sharp decline of demand.

accept: There has been a sharp decline in demand.

phrases.en: Profits remained steady throughout the year.
phrases.pt: Os lucros se mantiveram estáveis ao longo do ano.
phrases.note: Steady means stable, with little change.

examples: Profits remained steady throughout the year.
Attendance remained steady throughout the term.
Prices remained steady throughout the quarter.
pattern.contrast: Profits remained steady during of the year.

phrases.en: The numbers have plateaued recently.
phrases.pt: Os números estagnaram recentemente.
phrases.note: Plateau means to stop rising and stay flat.

pattern.slot: the measure, then when it flattened
examples: The numbers have plateaued recently.
Sign-ups have plateaued since March.
Sales have plateaued this quarter.
pattern.contrast: The numbers have plateau recently.

phrases.en: Costs are expected to rise gradually.
phrases.pt: Espera-se que os custos subam gradualmente.
phrases.note: States a forecast in a neutral tone.

pattern.slot: the measure, then the base verb
examples: Costs are expected to rise gradually.
Prices are expected to fall slightly.
Numbers are expected to recover slowly.
pattern.contrast: Costs are expected rise gradually.

phrases.en: This accounts for roughly half of revenue.
phrases.pt: Isso representa cerca de metade da receita.
phrases.note: Account for means to make up a share.

pattern.slot: the part, then the share it makes up
examples: This accounts for roughly half of revenue.
Shipping accounts for most of the cost.
That group accounts for a third of users.
pattern.contrast: This accounts roughly half of revenue.

phrases.en: The trend is likely to continue.
phrases.pt: É provável que a tendência continue.
phrases.note: Likely to shows strong probability.

pattern.slot: the subject, then the base verb
examples: The trend is likely to continue.
Demand is likely to fall.
The delay is likely to affect the launch.
pattern.contrast: The trend is likely continue.

phrases.en: Overall, the outlook is promising.
phrases.pt: No geral, a perspectiva é promissora.
phrases.note: Outlook means the expected future.

examples: Overall, the outlook is promising.
Overall, the results are encouraging.
Overall, the picture is mixed.
pattern.contrast: Overall of, the outlook is promising.

objective: Present figures and trends: describe rises, falls, and plateaus, and hedge a forecast appropriately.
pronunciationFocus: Gradable verbs carry the emotion: 'sales have SOARED', 'a SHARP decline' — lengthen the stressed vowel.
productionPrompt: Describe how a number you know (spending, followers, sales) has changed over the last year, and give a hedged forecast.
retryHint: Use one movement verb ('soared', 'declined', 'plateaued'), one hedge ('is expected to', 'is likely to'), and 'overall' for the summary.

dialogue.speaker: Priscila
dialogue.en: Sales have soared over the past quarter, up nearly thirty percent.
dialogue.pt: As vendas dispararam no último trimestre, quase trinta por cento a mais.

dialogue.speaker: Gil
dialogue.en: Across every region?
dialogue.pt: Em todas as regiões?

dialogue.speaker: Priscila
dialogue.en: No. Two regions drove it; in the north there's been a sharp decline in demand.
dialogue.pt: Não. Duas regiões puxaram; no norte houve uma queda acentuada na demanda.

dialogue.speaker: Gil
dialogue.en: What's the forecast?
dialogue.pt: Qual é a previsão?

dialogue.speaker: Priscila
dialogue.en: Costs are expected to rise gradually, but overall the outlook is promising.
dialogue.pt: Espera-se que os custos subam aos poucos, mas no geral a perspectiva é boa.

dialogue.speaker: Gil
dialogue.en: So the trend is likely to continue if we support the north.
dialogue.pt: Então a tendência deve continuar se a gente reforçar o norte.

comprehension.prompt: What is Priscila presenting?
options: Quarterly sales results and the forecast
comprehension.answer: Quarterly sales results and the forecast

comprehension.prompt: What is happening to demand in the north?
options: There has been a sharp decline
comprehension.answer: There has been a sharp decline

comprehension.prompt: What does Priscila expect costs to do?

title: Lesson 26 — Nuance and Stance
topic: Expressing precise attitudes and reservations

phrases.en: I would hesitate to call it a failure.
phrases.pt: Eu hesitaria em chamar isso de fracasso.
phrases.note: Use hesitate to soften a strong label.

pattern.slot: base verb: what you stop short of doing
examples: I would hesitate to call it a failure.
I would hesitate to draw a conclusion.
I would hesitate to generalise from one case.
pattern.contrast: I would hesitate in calling it a failure.

accept: I'd hesitate to call it a failure.

phrases.en: That said, the proposal still has considerable merit.
phrases.pt: Dito isso, a proposta ainda tem mérito considerável.
phrases.note: Signals a contrast while keeping balance.

pattern.slot: the qualifying claim, as a full clause
examples: That said, the proposal still has considerable merit.
That said, the timing is difficult.
That said, we should still test it.
pattern.contrast: That said that the proposal still has considerable merit.

phrases.en: There is a subtle but important distinction here.
phrases.pt: Há uma distinção sutil, mas importante aqui.
phrases.note: Useful for drawing fine conceptual lines.

pattern.frame: There is a subtle but important ___
pattern.slot: the noun that names the difference
examples: There is a subtle but important distinction here.
There is a subtle but important difference between them.
There is a subtle but important shift in the wording.
pattern.contrast: Exists a subtle but important distinction here.

accept: There's a subtle but important distinction here.

phrases.en: I am broadly sympathetic to that view.
phrases.pt: Eu tendo a simpatizar com essa visão em linhas gerais.
phrases.note: Shows partial agreement without full commitment.

pattern.slot: the stance you hold in general terms
examples: I am broadly sympathetic to that view.
I am broadly supportive of the plan.
I am broadly in agreement with the analysis.
pattern.contrast: I am broadly sympathetic with that view.

phrases.en: The evidence points in a different direction.
phrases.pt: As evidências apontam em outra direção.
phrases.note: A measured way to challenge a claim.

pattern.slot: where it points, and how firmly
examples: The evidence points in a different direction.
The evidence points to a slower effect.
The evidence points the other way.
pattern.contrast: The evidence points for a different direction.

phrases.en: It is not merely a matter of preference.
phrases.pt: Não é meramente uma questão de preferência.
phrases.note: Use merely to narrow or dismiss a simple explanation.

examples: It is not merely a matter of preference.
It is not merely a technical problem.
It is not merely a question of cost.
pattern.contrast: It is not merely only a matter of preference.

accept: It's not merely a matter of preference.

phrases.en: I take your point, but I remain unconvinced.
phrases.pt: Entendo seu ponto, mas continuo não convencido.
phrases.note: A polished way to disagree after acknowledging.

pattern.slot: your reservation, as a full clause
examples: I take your point, but I remain unconvinced.
I take your point, but the risk is still there.
I take your point, but I would sequence it differently.
pattern.contrast: I take your point, but however I remain unconvinced.

phrases.en: The issue is more complex than it first appears.
phrases.pt: A questão é mais complexa do que parece à primeira vista.
phrases.note: Introduces nuance before deeper explanation.

pattern.frame: ___ is more ___ than it first appears.
examples: The issue is more complex than it first appears.
The trade-off is more delicate than it first appears.
The question is more political than it first appears.
pattern.contrast: The issue is more complex of what it first appears.

objective: Register a precise degree of agreement or doubt, mark distinctions, and qualify a judgement without hedging into vagueness.
pronunciationFocus: Concessive discourse markers sit on their own tone unit: 'That said, —', 'I take your point, — but…'.
productionPrompt: Give a nuanced verdict on something you have mixed feelings about. Concede one real strength, then explain the reservation that still holds.
retryHint: Qualify with 'I would hesitate to…', concede with 'That said…', and hold your line with 'I take your point, but I remain unconvinced'.

dialogue.speaker: Halvor
dialogue.en: So your assessment is that the pilot failed?
dialogue.pt: Então sua avaliação é de que o piloto fracassou?

dialogue.speaker: Dela
dialogue.en: I would hesitate to call it a failure. That said, it clearly missed its main target.
dialogue.pt: Eu hesitaria em chamar de fracasso. Dito isso, ele claramente não atingiu o objetivo principal.

dialogue.speaker: Halvor
dialogue.en: The engagement numbers were strong, though.
dialogue.pt: Mas os números de engajamento foram bons.

dialogue.speaker: Dela
dialogue.en: There's a subtle but important distinction between engagement and retention. The evidence points in a different direction on retention.
dialogue.pt: Há uma distinção sutil, mas importante, entre engajamento e retenção. As evidências apontam para outra direção quanto à retenção.

dialogue.speaker: Halvor
dialogue.en: So you'd recommend against scaling it.
dialogue.pt: Então você recomendaria não expandir.

dialogue.speaker: Dela
dialogue.en: I take your point about the early signs, but I remain unconvinced. The issue is more complex than it first appears.
dialogue.pt: Entendo seu argumento sobre os primeiros sinais, mas continuo não convencida. A questão é mais complexa do que parece à primeira vista.

comprehension.prompt: What is Dela's overall stance on the pilot?
options: Cautiously negative — not a clear failure, but not ready to scale
Strongly positive — it should be expanded now
Completely neutral — the data says nothing useful
comprehension.answer: Cautiously negative — not a clear failure, but not ready to scale

comprehension.prompt: Which distinction does Dela emphasize?
How does Dela respond to Halvor's point about early signs?
options: She acknowledges it but stays unconvinced
comprehension.answer: She acknowledges it but stays unconvinced

title: Lesson 27 — Register and Professional Tone
topic: Adjusting tone in professional contexts

phrases.en: I wanted to follow up on our previous conversation.
phrases.pt: Eu queria dar continuidade à nossa conversa anterior.
phrases.note: A professional way to reopen a topic.

pattern.frame: I wanted to follow up on ___
examples: I wanted to follow up on our previous conversation.
I wanted to follow up on the action points.
I wanted to follow up on my last email.
pattern.contrast: I wanted follow up on our previous conversation.

phrases.en: Could you clarify what you mean by that?
phrases.pt: Você poderia esclarecer o que quer dizer com isso?
phrases.note: Direct but polite request for precision.

pattern.slot: what needs to be made precise
examples: Could you clarify what you mean by that?
Could you clarify the timeline?
Could you clarify which option you prefer?
pattern.contrast: Could you clarify me what you mean by that?

phrases.en: I appreciate the constraints you are working under.
phrases.pt: Eu entendo as restrições sob as quais você está trabalhando.
phrases.note: Shows empathy while discussing limits.

examples: I appreciate the constraints you are working under.
I appreciate the pressure the team is under.
I appreciate how quickly you replied.
pattern.contrast: I appreciate for the constraints you are working under.

phrases.en: Let me rephrase that more carefully.
phrases.pt: Deixe-me reformular isso com mais cuidado.
phrases.note: Useful when correcting your own wording.

pattern.slot: base verb: what you offer to do
examples: Let me rephrase that more carefully.
Let me put the other case.
Let me check the numbers first.
pattern.contrast: Let me to rephrase that more carefully.

phrases.en: From a practical standpoint, the timeline is tight.
phrases.pt: Do ponto de vista prático, o prazo está apertado.
phrases.note: Frames an opinion from a specific angle.

pattern.slot: the lens + the claim it supports
examples: From a practical standpoint, the timeline is tight.
From a legal standpoint, the wording matters.
From a commercial standpoint, the deal is thin.
pattern.contrast: From a practical standpoint of view, the timeline is tight.

phrases.en: I would not want to overstate the impact.
phrases.pt: Eu não gostaria de exagerar o impacto.
phrases.note: Prevents a claim from sounding too strong.

pattern.slot: base verb: what you are careful not to do
examples: I would not want to overstate the impact.
I would not want to pre-empt the review.
I would not want to speak for the team.
pattern.contrast: I would not want overstate the impact.

phrases.en: This may require a more coordinated approach.
phrases.pt: Isso talvez exija uma abordagem mais coordenada.
phrases.note: Sounds more strategic than simply saying plan.

examples: This may require a more coordinated approach.
This may require a second review.
This may require more time than we have.
pattern.contrast: This may require of a more coordinated approach.

phrases.en: Please let me know if I have misunderstood anything.
phrases.pt: Por favor, me avise se eu tiver entendido algo errado.
phrases.note: Keeps accountability while inviting correction.

examples: Please let me know if I have misunderstood anything.
Please let me know if that works for you.
Let me know if you need anything else.
pattern.contrast: Please let me to know if I have misunderstood anything.

objective: Raise a difficult point in a professional register: soften requests, acknowledge the other side's position, and invite correction.
pronunciationFocus: Polite formulas stay level and unstressed until the content word: 'I wanted to follow up on our previous conVERSAtion'.
productionPrompt: Deliver bad news to a client or manager in a professional tone. Acknowledge their position, explain the cause, and commit to a next step.
retryHint: Open with 'I wanted to follow up on…', acknowledge with 'I appreciate the constraints you're working under', and hedge with 'I wouldn't want to overstate…'.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Adeyemi
dialogue.en: Your team said the report would be ready last week.
dialogue.pt: Sua equipe disse que o relatório estaria pronto na semana passada.

dialogue.speaker: Pieter
dialogue.en: I wanted to follow up on that. From a practical standpoint, the timeline turned out to be tight.
dialogue.pt: Eu queria retomar isso. Do ponto de vista prático, o prazo acabou ficando apertado.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Adeyemi
dialogue.en: Tight because of what, exactly?
dialogue.pt: Apertado por causa de quê, exatamente?

dialogue.speaker: Pieter
dialogue.en: Let me rephrase that more carefully. We received the final data three days late, which moved everything.
dialogue.pt: Deixa eu reformular com mais cuidado. Recebemos os dados finais com três dias de atraso, o que deslocou tudo.

dialogue.speaker: Mrs. Adeyemi
dialogue.en: I appreciate that, but I need a firm date.
dialogue.pt: Eu entendo, mas preciso de uma data firme.

dialogue.speaker: Pieter
dialogue.en: Thursday. I would not want to overstate our certainty, but Thursday is realistic. Please tell me if I've misunderstood the priority.
dialogue.pt: Quinta-feira. Eu não gostaria de exagerar nossa certeza, mas quinta é realista. Por favor, me diga se entendi errado a prioridade.

comprehension.prompt: What is the purpose of Pieter's message?
options: To explain a delayed report and commit to a new date
To end the contract with the client
To ask the client for more money
comprehension.answer: To explain a delayed report and commit to a new date

comprehension.prompt: What reason does Pieter give for the delay?
options: The final data arrived three days late
comprehension.answer: The final data arrived three days late

comprehension.prompt: How does Pieter present the new date?
options: As realistic, without overstating his certainty
As a firm guarantee with no risk
comprehension.answer: As realistic, without overstating his certainty

title: Lesson 28 — Precision and Emphasis
topic: Making exact claims with controlled emphasis

phrases.en: The distinction is not incidental; it is central.
phrases.pt: A distinção não é incidental; ela é central.
phrases.note: Uses contrast to emphasize importance.

pattern.slot: the thing + the weak reading you reject + the strong one
examples: The distinction is not incidental; it is central.
The delay is not accidental; it is structural.
The choice is not technical; it is political.
pattern.contrast: The distinction is not incidental; is central.

accept: The distinction is not incidental; it's central.

phrases.en: That interpretation strikes me as overly reductive.
phrases.pt: Essa interpretação me parece excessivamente reducionista.
phrases.note: A sophisticated way to present a judgment.

pattern.slot: the claim + your judgement of it
examples: That interpretation strikes me as overly reductive.
That framing strikes me as too neat.
The comparison strikes me as unfair.
pattern.contrast: That interpretation strikes me like overly reductive.

phrases.en: We should avoid conflating correlation with causation.
phrases.pt: Devemos evitar confundir correlação com causalidade.
phrases.note: Conflate means to wrongly treat two things as one.

examples: We should avoid conflating correlation with causation.
We should avoid conflating popularity with quality.
We should avoid conflating a symptom with a cause.
pattern.contrast: We should avoid to conflate correlation with causation.

phrases.en: The claim holds only under very specific conditions.
phrases.pt: A afirmação se sustenta apenas sob condições muito específicas.
phrases.note: Restricts a claim with precision.

examples: The claim holds only under very specific conditions.
The claim holds only for the first cohort.
The claim holds only if the price stays fixed.
pattern.contrast: The claim holds only under very specifics conditions.

phrases.en: This is less a contradiction than a shift in emphasis.
phrases.pt: Isso é menos uma contradição do que uma mudança de ênfase.
phrases.note: Reframes how the listener should interpret something.

pattern.slot: the overstated reading + the accurate one
examples: This is less a contradiction than a shift in emphasis.
This is less a disagreement than a difference in scope.
This is less a failure than an unfinished experiment.
pattern.contrast: This is less a contradiction of a shift in emphasis.

phrases.en: The wording leaves room for considerable ambiguity.
phrases.pt: A formulação deixa espaço para uma ambiguidade considerável.
phrases.note: Useful for critiquing imprecise language.

pattern.slot: the text + what it lets through
examples: The wording leaves room for considerable ambiguity.
The clause leaves room for a much wider reading.
The summary leaves room for doubt.
pattern.contrast: The wording leaves room to considerable ambiguity.

phrases.en: I would frame the problem somewhat differently.
phrases.pt: Eu enquadraria o problema de uma forma um pouco diferente.
phrases.note: Frame means define how an issue is understood.

pattern.slot: what you would reframe, and by how much
examples: I would frame the problem somewhat differently.
I would frame the question differently.
I would frame the trade-off somewhat differently.
pattern.contrast: I would frame the problem of a somewhat different way.

accept: I'd frame the problem somewhat differently.

phrases.en: The conclusion follows, but only with several caveats.
phrases.pt: A conclusão procede, mas apenas com várias ressalvas.
phrases.note: Adds limitations to a conclusion.

examples: The conclusion follows, but only with several caveats.
The conclusion follows, but only for this sample.
The conclusion follows, but only if we accept the premise.
pattern.contrast: The conclusion follows, but only with severals caveats.

objective: Make an exact claim: bound it with conditions, separate it from a near neighbour, and place emphasis deliberately rather than by volume.
pronunciationFocus: Emphasis by contrast, not force: drop pitch on 'not incidental', lift it on 'it is CENtral' — the fall-rise carries the weight.
productionPrompt: State a claim you believe is often oversimplified. Bound it with the conditions under which it holds, and name the near neighbour it gets confused with.
retryHint: Use 'X is less a … than a …', 'it holds only under specific conditions', and 'the conclusion follows, but only with several caveats'.

dialogue.speaker: Anselm
dialogue.en: Your draft treats the two studies as saying the same thing.
dialogue.pt: Seu rascunho trata os dois estudos como se dissessem a mesma coisa.

dialogue.speaker: Idil
dialogue.en: That interpretation strikes me as overly reductive. This is less a contradiction than a shift in emphasis.
dialogue.pt: Essa interpretação me parece redutora demais. Isso é menos uma contradição do que uma mudança de ênfase.

dialogue.speaker: Anselm
dialogue.en: Then say so explicitly. As written, the wording leaves room for considerable ambiguity.
dialogue.pt: Então diga isso de forma explícita. Como está, a redação deixa margem para uma ambiguidade considerável.

dialogue.speaker: Idil
dialogue.en: Fair. I'd frame the problem somewhat differently in the revision.
dialogue.pt: Justo. Eu formularia o problema de um jeito um pouco diferente na revisão.

dialogue.speaker: Anselm
dialogue.en: And the causal claim in paragraph four?
dialogue.pt: E a afirmação causal no parágrafo quatro?

dialogue.speaker: Idil
dialogue.en: It holds only under specific conditions. The conclusion follows, but only with several caveats, which I'll add.
dialogue.pt: Ela se sustenta apenas sob condições específicas. A conclusão se segue, mas só com várias ressalvas, que eu vou acrescentar.

comprehension.prompt: What is the editorial disagreement about?
options: How precisely the draft states its claims
Whether to publish the article at all
comprehension.answer: How precisely the draft states its claims

comprehension.prompt: How does Idil characterize the relationship between the two studies?
options: A shift in emphasis rather than a contradiction
comprehension.answer: A shift in emphasis rather than a contradiction

comprehension.prompt: What does Idil agree to do about the causal claim?
options: Add the caveats and conditions it depends on
comprehension.answer: Add the caveats and conditions it depends on

title: Lesson 29 — Rhetorical Control
topic: Controlling argument flow and emphasis

phrases.en: Let us not lose sight of the broader question.
phrases.pt: Não percamos de vista a questão mais ampla.
phrases.note: Redirects attention to the main issue.

pattern.frame: Let us not lose sight of ___
examples: Let us not lose sight of the broader question.
Let us not lose sight of the original aim.
Let us not lose sight of who bears the cost.
pattern.contrast: Let us not lose the sight of the broader question.

phrases.en: The real issue lies elsewhere.
phrases.pt: A verdadeira questão está em outro lugar.
phrases.note: Moves the discussion away from a false focus.

examples: The real issue lies elsewhere.
The real issue lies upstream.
The real issue lies in how the target was chosen.
pattern.contrast: The real issue lies in elsewhere.

phrases.en: It is worth pausing over that assumption.
phrases.pt: Vale a pena nos determos nessa suposição.
phrases.note: Slows the argument to inspect a premise.

examples: It is worth pausing over that assumption.
It is worth asking who benefits.
It is worth separating the two claims.
pattern.contrast: It is worth to pause over that assumption.

accept: It's worth pausing over that assumption.

phrases.en: That may be true, but it does not settle the matter.
phrases.pt: Isso pode ser verdade, mas não resolve a questão.
phrases.note: Concedes a point without accepting the conclusion.

examples: That may be true, but it does not settle the matter.
That may be true, but it changes little in practice.
That may be true, but the question was different.
pattern.contrast: That may be true, but however it does not settle the matter.

phrases.en: The argument gains force when viewed in context.
phrases.pt: O argumento ganha força quando visto em contexto.
phrases.note: Explains why context strengthens a claim.

pattern.slot: the claim + the condition that strengthens it
examples: The argument gains force when viewed in context.
The objection gains force when the costs are counted.
The comparison gains force when both cases are old.
pattern.contrast: The argument gains force when is viewed in context.

phrases.en: I do not think that objection is decisive.
phrases.pt: Não acho que essa objeção seja decisiva.
phrases.note: Acknowledges an objection but limits its impact.

pattern.slot: the claim + the property you deny it
examples: I do not think that objection is decisive.
I do not think the evidence is conclusive.
I do not think the comparison is fair.
pattern.contrast: I do not think that objection is not decisive.

phrases.en: The broader implication is hard to ignore.
phrases.pt: A implicação mais ampla é difícil de ignorar.
phrases.note: Draws attention to consequences beyond the details.

examples: The broader implication is hard to ignore.
The broader implication is uncomfortable.
The broader implication is that the rule needs rewriting.
pattern.contrast: The broader implication is hard of ignore.

phrases.en: This brings us back to the central tension.
phrases.pt: Isso nos traz de volta à tensão central.
phrases.note: Returns the discussion to its core conflict.

pattern.slot: the point you are returning to
examples: This brings us back to the central tension.
This brings us back to the original question.
This brings us back to who decides.
pattern.contrast: This brings us back at the central tension.

objective: Control the shape of an argument in real time: redirect attention, rank objections by weight, and return the discussion to its core.
pronunciationFocus: Structural signposts take a full pause on both sides: 'That may be true — but it does not settle the matter'.
productionPrompt: Take a discussion that has drifted onto a minor point and steer it back. Concede the small point, name the real issue, and state the central tension.
retryHint: Use 'That may be true, but it does not settle the matter', 'The real issue lies elsewhere', and 'This brings us back to the central tension'.

dialogue.speaker: Bório
dialogue.en: You're spending too long on the funding figure. It's a rounding error.
dialogue.pt: Você está demorando demais na cifra do financiamento. É um erro de arredondamento.

dialogue.speaker: Wen
dialogue.en: That may be true, but it does not settle the matter. The real issue lies elsewhere — in who controls the timeline.
dialogue.pt: Isso pode ser verdade, mas não resolve a questão. O problema de fato está em outro lugar — em quem controla o cronograma.

dialogue.speaker: Bório
dialogue.en: The timeline objection has been raised before and dismissed.
dialogue.pt: A objeção sobre o cronograma já foi levantada antes e descartada.

dialogue.speaker: Wen
dialogue.en: I don't think that objection is decisive. Viewed in the context of the last two delays, the argument gains force.
dialogue.pt: Não acho que essa objeção seja decisiva. Vista no contexto dos dois últimos atrasos, a tese ganha força.

dialogue.speaker: Bório
dialogue.en: So what do you want the committee to take away?
dialogue.pt: Então o que você quer que o comitê leve daqui?

dialogue.speaker: Wen
dialogue.en: Let us not lose sight of the broader question. This brings us back to the central tension: speed against oversight.
dialogue.pt: Não vamos perder de vista a questão mais ampla. Isso nos traz de volta à tensão central: velocidade contra supervisão.

comprehension.prompt: What is Wen trying to do in this exchange?
options: Redirect the discussion to what she sees as the core issue
Concede that the funding figure decides everything
End the meeting without a conclusion
comprehension.answer: Redirect the discussion to what she sees as the core issue

comprehension.prompt: What does Wen say is the real issue?
Why does Wen think the timeline objection now gains force?
options: Seen in the context of the last two delays
comprehension.answer: Seen in the context of the last two delays

title: Extra A1 — Weather and Clothes
topic: Weather, clothes, and simple daily choices

phrases.en: It's sunny today.
phrases.pt: Hoje está ensolarado.
phrases.note: Use it is to describe the weather.

examples: It's sunny today.
It's cold today.
It's windy today.
pattern.contrast: It's sun today.

accept: It is sunny today.

phrases.en: It's raining now.
phrases.pt: Está chovendo agora.
phrases.note: Use is plus raining for weather happening now.

pattern.slot: -ing verb: what the weather is doing
examples: It's raining now.
It's snowing now.
It's clearing up now.
pattern.contrast: It's rain now.

accept: It is raining now.

phrases.en: It's cold outside.
phrases.pt: Está frio lá fora.
phrases.note: Outside means not inside a building.

examples: It's cold outside.
It's hot outside.
It's dark outside.
pattern.contrast: It's does cold outside.

accept: It is cold outside.

phrases.en: I need a jacket.
phrases.pt: Eu preciso de uma jaqueta.
phrases.note: Use I need for something necessary.

examples: I need help.
I need a jacket.
I need two tickets.
I need a short break.
pattern.contrast: I need of help.

phrases.en: I'm wearing a blue shirt.
phrases.pt: Estou usando uma camisa azul.
phrases.note: Use wearing for clothes on your body now.

examples: I'm wearing a blue shirt.
I'm wearing a coat.
I'm wearing my new shoes.
pattern.contrast: I'm wearing blue shirt.

phrases.en: Do I need an umbrella?
phrases.pt: Eu preciso de um guarda-chuva?
phrases.note: Put do before I to ask about a need.

examples: Do I need an umbrella?
Do I need a ticket?
Do I need to book?
pattern.contrast: I need an umbrella?

phrases.en: The weather is changing.
phrases.pt: O tempo está mudando.
phrases.note: Changing means becoming different.

pattern.slot: what the weather is doing, as an -ing verb
examples: The weather is changing.

The weather is improving.
pattern.contrast: The weather is change.

phrases.en: Let's stay inside.
phrases.pt: Vamos ficar dentro de casa.
phrases.note: Let's makes a suggestion for you and another person.

examples: Let's stay inside.
Let's try it together.
Let's take the bus.
pattern.contrast: Let's to stay inside.

objective: Talk about today's weather and choose the right clothes.
pronunciationFocus: Blend it is into IT'S: IT'S sunny today; IT'S cold outside.

dialogue.speaker: Tom
dialogue.en: Good morning, Bia. Is it cold outside?
dialogue.pt: Bom dia, Bia. Está frio lá fora?

dialogue.speaker: Bia
dialogue.en: It's sunny today, but it's cold outside.

title: Extra B1 — Learning Habits
topic: Explaining study routines and learning strategies

phrases.en: I learn faster when I use examples.

examples: I learn faster when I use examples.

pattern.contrast: I learn faster when I will use examples.

phrases.pt: Eu tento revisar um pouco todos os dias.
phrases.note: Try to introduces an effort or habit.

pattern.slot: base verb: the habit you aim for
examples: I try to review a little every day.

pattern.contrast: I try review a little every day.

phrases.en: Writing things down helps me remember them.
phrases.pt: Anotar as coisas me ajuda a lembrá-las.
phrases.note: An activity ending in -ing can be the subject of a sentence.

pattern.slot: -ing activity, then the base verb it helps with

pattern.contrast: Write things down helps me to remember them.

phrases.en: I lose focus if the session is too long.
